title: Kafka Producers and Consumers
summary: Understand topics and groups before configuring and writing a producer and a listener.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: What is Kafka ? How to use Confluent Kafka in Spring Boot Application ?

richText: Publish and read records
Kafka stores records so other parts of an application can process them later.
A producer publishes records. A consumer reads and processes them.
A topic is a named collection of records. A broker is a Kafka server that stores them.
A topic has partitions. Each partition stores records in order.
An offset is a record’s position in its partition. Kafka guarantees ordering within a partition.
A consumer group shares a topic’s partitions among its consumers. Each partition is assigned to one consumer in that group at a time.
A separate group can read the same topic independently.
Use Kafka for delayed work, persistent backlogs, or events needed by multiple services.
Configure the record format
Add spring-kafka and let Spring Boot manage its compatible version.
A serializer converts a Java value into bytes. A deserializer converts the received bytes into a Java value.
The producer and consumer must agree on the record format.
Define an event ID and a format version so consumers can identify repeated records and understand changed fields.
bootstrap-servers gives the client initial broker addresses.
For Confluent Cloud, use the supplied addresses, credentials, and SASL_SSL settings. SASL authenticates the client and SSL encrypts the connection.

example.title: Configure string keys and JSON text values
description: Use Spring Boot 3, Spring Kafka 3+, and Java 17.
Set KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS and add these settings to application.properties.
A local broker can use localhost:9092. A cloud broker also needs its provider authentication settings.
explanation: StringSerializer and StringDeserializer handle both keys and values as text.
The application puts JSON inside the value string. Kafka does not validate that JSON contract.
enable-auto-commit=false leaves offset commits to the listener container.
earliest applies when the group has no valid committed offset. It does not replay all records on every restart.

richText: Publish a record
KafkaTemplate publishes records from Spring code.
A record key normally keeps related records in the same partition while the partition count and partitioning configuration remain unchanged.
In Spring Kafka 3+, send returns a CompletableFuture for the publish result.
Calling send does not by itself mean that the broker acknowledged the record. Inspect the future or attach a completion callback.
Broker acknowledgment confirms publication according to the producer settings. It does not mean that a consumer completed its work.

get waits up to five seconds for the send result.
The result provides the offset assigned by Kafka.
A timeout stops the wait. The publish may still complete afterward.

richText: Process records in a listener
@KafkaListener registers a bean method that receives records from a topic.
The group ID identifies the consumer group. Members of the same group share the work.
After successful processing, the container can commit offsets according to its acknowledgment policy.
A committed offset records how far the group has progressed.
Let processing exceptions reach the listener container so its retry and recovery policy can run.
A crash after an external action but before offset commit can cause that action to run again after redelivery.
